claim: Prompted as a single Black woman on Medicaid with a household income under $35,000, GPT-4o-mini returns a PHQ-8 total of 8 on its first draw, a plausible answer in the mild band.
Over thirty draws the same prompt averages 10.3.
Adults in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) who share her race, sex, income and marital status average 4.7.

The worked example applies the ladder to 28,800 PHQ-8 depression assessments from GPT-4o-mini, Gemini-3-Flash, DeepSeek-V3 and GLM-4.7, a corpus first collected for an earlier audit [keough2026plausible] and rebuilt here from the raw answers.
Four models, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini-3-Flash, DeepSeek-V3 and GLM-4.7, generated the corpus through OpenRouter between 28 December 2025 and 11 January 2026.
The corpus holds 28,800 assessments, of which 28,799 have a valid PHQ-8.

For the population reference we use the 36,274 adults in NHANES 2005–2018 who answered all eight PHQ-8 items, analysed with the survey's weights and design [johnson2013nhanes,chen2018nhanes,nchs2018analytic].
On this corpus the NHANES standard deviation of the PHQ-8 total sets the gate tolerances at 0.98 and 0.49 points and the default level-3 tolerance at about 2 points.
Scored against the whole survey, no NHANES subgroup by sex, race and ethnicity, income or survey cycle departs from 1 by more than a factor of 1.36, so level 1 uses tau = 1.5.

The draw-to-draw standard deviation is 1.25 to 2.24 points in every model and framing, above the 0.98-point tolerance.
Averages of 30 draws pass in every model, and the minimum rule needs 3 to 6 draws.
Two draws of one persona fall in different PHQ-8 severity bands 35.2% of the time [33.6, 36.8].
In a separate decoding control on 12 personas, setting GPT-4o-mini's temperature to 0 cut its draw variance to 12.5% of the default without separating personas any better (Supplement S1.10).
No model passes level 1, in either framing or at any tolerance up to 3.
At matched totals NHANES puts 5% of adults in each tail of person fit, and the models put 0.0% to 1.0% in the unusual tail and 0.0% to 4.3% in the regular tail.

The models also weight depressed mood more heavily than people do, scoring 0.16 to 0.51 points higher at matched totals on depressed mood and 0.22 to 1.11 points lower on fatigue, one of the physical symptoms people report first.
They reuse answer sheets as well, giving two different personas the identical answer vector 4.6 to 39 times as often as two NHANES adults with the same total.
The gap between low- and high-income personas is 1.91 (DeepSeek-V3) to 5.07 (Gemini-3-Flash) times the population gap.
Of the 12 per-model income contrasts, 10 are steepened, and the survey measures the other two gaps too imprecisely to certify kept.
We read the size of the low-to-high ratio as partly a product of how the persona's income label is matched to the survey.

Matching on the dollar amount in the label (Supplement S3) brings the ratio down to 1.04 for DeepSeek-V3 and 1.18 for GPT-4o-mini, which leaves both contrasts unresolved, and Gemini-3-Flash and GLM-4.7 stay steepened at 2.76 and 2.74.
Under that matching DeepSeek-V3 and GPT-4o-mini still steepen the middle-to-high gap (3.29 and 2.89), leaving every model failing level 2.
On the sex gap the models disagree, with GPT-4o-mini and DeepSeek-V3 reproducing a quarter to two fifths of it (ratios 0.23 and 0.41), GLM-4.7 doubling it (2.06) and Gemini-3-Flash unresolved.
Pooled over the four models the ratio is 0.97, a near match built from errors in opposite directions.

Among adults matched on income, sex and marital status, the survey cannot tell the Hispanic–White gap from zero and measures the Black–White gap too imprecisely to certify kept, and GPT-4o-mini's Black–White gap is still not kept.
After reweighting, the overall residual is +2.1 points for GLM-4.7, +2.6 for Gemini-3-Flash, +4.6 for DeepSeek-V3 and +4.7 for GPT-4o-mini.
All 40 model-by-group residuals are positive, and no model passes all ten groups at 2 points.
In every model the largest residual is in the low-income band.
The failure holds under all eight reference specifications, including NHANES 2021–2023, and only whether the national row passes depends on the reference chosen (Supplement S3).
In the low-income band 55.5% of simulated respondents score 10 or more, against 13.6% of real adults.

Across the middle and high bands the simulated share is too low although the mean is too high, and DeepSeek-V3's overall prevalence looks correct only because its low-income excess cancels these shortfalls.
DeepSeek-V3 and GPT-4o-mini have no general factor, with first-to-second eigenvalue ratios of 1.09 to 1.73 against 7.47 in NHANES.
Gemini-3-Flash and GLM-4.7 have a factor with the human pattern of loadings (congruence .990 to .998), and the loadings are stronger than people's.
Gemini-3-Flash fails R2 in both framings and GLM-4.7 in the narrative framing, and both fail invariance across income, which holds in NHANES.
In these two models 48% to 64% of item variance lies between personas, against 3.5% between demographic cells in NHANES, and draws of one persona share no general factor.
She is a single Black woman on Medicaid with an income under $35,000, and GPT-4o-mini gives her 30 clinical draws ranging from 7 to 16.
Her first draw of 8 lands in the mild band and her mean of 10.3 in the moderate band, so her readable score is the average.
Her 60 draws are each plausible as human answers and together less varied than real people at her severity, repeating the level 1 failure.
Her mean over both framings, 10.0, exceeds the 4.7 of matched NHANES adults by 5.3 points, repeating the level 3 excess.

When a prompt control on 12 personas (Supplement S1.9) asked each model to answer as the person described, DeepSeek-V3 and GPT-4o-mini scored 5.8 to 7.4 points above NHANES in every income band, compared with 4.0 to 5.3 under the corpus prompt, while Gemini-3-Flash's low-income excess grew from 8.9 to 10.0 points.
Run on the real corpus with the full reference, the control code reproduces all 303 published rung numbers.
Real respondents pass the gate and level 3 in every reading, level 1 in 92.9% of replicates, and R1 and R2 of level 4 in every replicate, and level 2 fails them in no reading (Table 3).
At 30 draws real respondents' persona means reach a dependability of only .70, because real demographic cells differ little from one another.
Each planted failure trips the rung it targets.
Independent items fail level 1, R1 and R2 in every replicate, and compressed samples fail level 1 in every replicate.
Shifted samples fail level 3 in every reading, and non-invariant samples fail R4 in all 25 replicates.
A doubled income gap fails level 2 in 92.5% of per-model readings.
A sample shifted by 2.1 points passes the gate in only 28.6% of readings, as more depressed respondents vary more between draws.
In those replicates real respondents' misfit ratio averages 1.15, and level 1 passes them at tau = 1.5 in 99.4% of 800 per-model readings, which sets the level-1 floor.
A second simulation repeated the control panel over 60 replicates on grids of 48, 144 and 432 persona cells.
Level 2 fails a faithful simulator built from real respondents in at most 3.3% of per-model readings and fails a doubled income gap in 97.5% to 100%.
At 30 draws per persona the low-to-high income gap of a faithful simulator is never read kept, because draws of one persona vary enough to hold its interval wider than the kept region.
With no simulation error, the limit of adding draws, the same gap is read kept in 95.0% and 98.3% of replicates on the 48-cell and 144-cell grids.
The Black–White and Hispanic–White gaps are never read kept on any grid, because NHANES measures them too loosely.

R4 shows the same asymmetry, and at the .08 margin, 24 to 40 personas per group leave some invariance steps unresolved for real respondents in 24 of 25 replicates, while a planted invariance failure fails R4 in every replicate.

[bisbee2024synthetic] gave ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo, June 2023) the profiles of 7,530 respondents to the 2016 and 2020 American National Election Studies and asked, about 30 times under each of three prompts, for a feeling thermometer toward each of 11 groups.
Our cleaning of the released file reproduces the authors' analysis data and their published regression to six decimals.
The gate passes for every thermometer, with at most 11 draws needed under the recommended rule, and level 2 fails under every prompt.

Under the full prompt, 3 of the 77 contrasts are kept, among them the partisan gaps in feeling toward the Democratic and Republican parties (ratios 1.12 and 1.05), both large and precisely measured in the survey.
The Republican–Democrat gap is steepened toward five other groups, and several gaps by sex and age are reversed, missing or attenuated.
Level 3 passes at half a standard deviation for 7 of the 11 thermometers under the full prompt.
In their Study 3, [argyle2023outofone] gave GPT-3 each of 4,270 American National Election Studies respondents' answers to 11 of 12 interview questions and asked it to answer the twelfth.
Of 61 contrasts in the main run, 2 are kept, the Republican–Democrat gaps in ideology and in Trump's two-party vote share (both 0.92).
Nine are not kept, among them the Black–White gap in Trump's vote share, which GPT-3 reproduces at about half its size (0.53).
Most of the remaining contrasts are not read, because the survey's subgroups are too small to measure their gaps.
Of the 154 contrasts across models, elicitation methods and steering methods, 1 is kept, 33 are not kept, 115 are unresolved and 5 are not read.
A comparison of point estimates would credit far more fidelity than the data establish, with the point ratio inside the kept region for 37 of the 149 contrasts read.
The ladder keeps 1 of those 37 and reports the other 36 as unresolved, and a researcher using these releases can claim little about group gaps in either direction.

Additionally, the researcher fixes how each persona attribute maps to a reference variable before generation and reports that mapping with the verdicts, because in the worked example matching income on the label's dollar amount rather than the poverty-ratio band changed the verdict on one contrast.
Across 28,800 PHQ-8 assessments from four models, the ladder read every model's persona means and failed every model on each use above them.
